sanskrit: samutpatantu pradiśo nabhasvatīḥ sam abhrāṇi vātajūtāni yantu | maharṣabhasya nadato nabhasvato vāśrā āpaḥ pṛthivīṃ tarpayantu ||
english: Let the quarters of the sky, cloud-bearing, fly up together; let the clouds driven by the wind come together. Let the roaring waters of the great bull, cloud-laden, resounding, refresh the earth.

sanskrit: sam īkṣayati viṣvagvāto nabhāṃsy apāṃ vegāsaḥ pṛthag ut patantu | varṣasya sargā mahayantu bhūmiṃ pṛthag jāyantām oṣadhayo viśvarūpāḥ ||
english: The all-pervading wind surveys the clouds; let the rushing torrents of waters rise up in every direction. Let the streams of rain magnify the earth; let the plants of every form spring up in their diversity.

sanskrit: abhi kranda stanayārdayodadhiṃ bhūmiṃ parjanya payasā sam aṅdhi | tvayā varṣaṃ bahulam etu sṛṣṭam āśāraiṣī kṛśagur etv astam ||
english: Thunder forth, O Parjanya, shake the ocean with your roar; saturate the earth with your milk. Through you let the rain be sent forth in abundance; let the lean cow seeking fodder come home.

sanskrit: ud īrayata marutaḥ samudratas tveṣā arkā nabha ut pātayantu | pra varṣayanti taviṣāḥ sudānavo 'pāṃ rasair oṣadhayaḥ sacantām ||
english: Stir up, O Maruts, from the ocean; let the blazing hymns send the clouds flying upward. The mighty, bounteous ones pour forth rain; let the plants be attended by the essences of the waters.

sanskrit: gaṇās tvopa gāyantu mārutāḥ parjanya ghoṣiṇaḥ pṛthak | sargā varṣasya varṣataḥ sṛjantu pṛthivīm abhi ||
english: Let the Marut-hosts sing out to you, O Parjanya, thundering one by one in their distinct voices. Let the streams of the raining rain pour forth over the earth.

sanskrit: sam avantu sudānava utsā ajagarā uta | vātā varṣasya varṣataḥ pra vāntu pṛthivīm anu ||
english: Let the bounteous ones flow together — the springs and the serpentine water-courses. Let the winds of the raining rain blow forth along the earth.

sanskrit: vāto vidyud abhraṃ varṣaṃ sam avantu sudānavaḥ | pra pyāyasva pra pinvasva saṃ bhūmiṃ payasā sṛja ||
english: Wind, lightning, cloud, and rain — let the bounteous ones come together. Swell forth, fill out; pour together with milk upon the earth.

sanskrit: apām agnis tanūbhiḥ saṃvidāno ya oṣadhīnām adhipā babhūva | sa no varṣaṃ vanutāṃ jātavedāḥ prāṇaṃ prajābhyo amṛtaṃ divas pari ||
english: Agni, united with the bodies of the waters, who became the lord of the plants — may Jātavedas, the All-knower, win rain for us, the breath of life, the immortal drink, from heaven, for our offspring.

sanskrit: āśām-āśāṃ vi dyotatāṃ vātā vāntu diśo-diśaḥ | marudbhiḥ pracyutā meghā varṣantu pṛthivīm abhi ||
english: Let lightning flash in every direction; let the winds blow from all quarters. Let the clouds, set in motion by the Maruts, rain down upon the earth.

sanskrit: prajāpatiḥ salilād ā samudrād āpa īrayann udadhim ardayāti | pra pyāyatāṃ vṛṣṇo aśvasya reto 'rvāṅ etena stanayitnunehy apo niṣiñcann asuraḥ pitā naḥ ||
english: Prajāpati, stirring up the waters from the primordial flood, from the ocean, agitates the sea. Let the seed of the virile horse swell forth; come hither, our father, the mighty Asura, pouring down the waters with this thunder.

sanskrit: śvasantu gargarā apām ava nīcīr apaḥ sṛja | vadantu pṛśnibāhavo maṇḍūkā īriṇānu ||
english: Let the gurgling whirlpools of the waters breathe; send down the waters below. Let the frogs with their speckled arms speak out along the pools.

sanskrit: saṃvatsaraṃ śaśayānā brāhmaṇā vratacāriṇaḥ | vācaṃ parjanyajinvatāṃ pra maṇḍūkā avādiṣuḥ ||
english: Having lain dormant for a year, like Brahmaṇas who observe their vow, the frogs have spoken forth, quickened into voice by Parjanya.

sanskrit: upapravada maṇḍūki varṣam ā vada tāduri | madhye hradasya plavasva vigṛhya caturaḥ padaḥ ||
english: Speak up, O little frog; speak the rain aloud, O tāduri-frog. Float in the middle of the pond, spreading out your four limbs.

sanskrit: mahāntaṃ kośam ud acābhi ṣiñca savidyutaṃ bhavatu vātu vātaḥ | tanvatāṃ yajñaṃ bahudhā visṛṣṭam ānandinīr oṣadhayo bhavantu ||
english: Draw up the great treasury and sprinkle it; let there be lightning, let the wind blow. Let them extend the sacrifice released in manifold ways; let the plants be filled with gladness.

sanskrit: yāvatī dyāvāpṛthivī varimṇā yāvad vā sapta sindhavo vitaṣṭhuḥ | vācaṃ viṣasya dūṣaṇīṃ tām ito nir avādiṣam ||
english: As wide as heaven and earth in their expanse, as far as the seven rivers extend — the utterance that corrupts the poison I have now spoken forth from here.

sanskrit: suparṇas tvā garutmān viṣa prathamam āvayat | nāropayo nāmādaya utāsmā abhavat pituḥ ||
english: Suparṇa, the winged Garutmān, first carried you, O poison. He neither brought you up nor tasted you, and yet he became its father.

sanskrit: yāṃ tvāsthat pañcāṅgulir vakrāc cid adhi dhanvanaḥ | apaskambhasya bāhvor nir avocam ahaṃ viṣam ||
english: That poison which the five-fingered one placed upon you, even upon the curved part of the bow — from the arms of Apaskambha I have spoken the poison forth.

sanskrit: śalyād viṣaṃ nir avocam añjanāt parṇadher uta | apāṣṭhāc chṛṅgāt kurmalān nir avocam ahaṃ viṣam ||
english: From the arrow-shaft I have spoken the poison forth, and from the collyrium, and from the quiver likewise. From the tail-fin, from the horn, from the kurmal plant — I have spoken the poison forth.

sanskrit: arasas ta iṣo śalyo 'tho te 'rasaṃ viṣam | utārasasya vṛkṣasya dhanuṣ ṭe arasārasam ||
english: Sapless is your dart, the arrow-shaft, and likewise sapless is your poison. And of the sapless tree, your bow is utterly devoid of potency.

sanskrit: ye +'pīṣan ye 'dihan ya āsyan ye 'vāsṛjan | sarve te vadhrayaḥ santu vadhrir viṣagiriṣ kṛtaḥ ||
english: Those who ground it, those who smeared it on, those who shot it, those who let it fly — may they all be castrated. The poison-mountain is made castrate.

sanskrit: vadhrayas te khanitāro vadhris tvam asy oṣadhe | vadhriḥ sa parvato girir yato jātam idaṃ viṣam ||
english: Castrated are your diggers; castrated you yourself are, O herb. Castrated is that mountain, that hill, from which this poison was born.

sanskrit: vār idaṃ vārayātai varuṇāvata ābhṛtam | tatrāmṛtasyāsiktaṃ tac cakārārasaṃ viṣam ||
english: This water — let it ward off what must be warded off; it has been brought from the realm of Varuṇa. There, where amṛta has been poured in, that has rendered the poison sapless.

sanskrit: khādireṇa śalilena- -atho kaṅkatadantyā | atho viṣasya yad viṣaṃ tena pāpīr anīnaśam ||
english: With the khadira-wood comb, with the water therein, and with the teeth of the kaṅkata-comb — with that which is the very poison of the poison, I have destroyed the evil ones.

sanskrit: kityā śataparvaṇā sahasrākṣeṇa carmaṇā | tīkṣṇābhir abhribhir vayaṃ nir ajāmaḥ sadānvāḥ ||
english: With the kiti-plant of a hundred joints, with the thousand-eyed hide, with sharp digging-spades we drive out the sadānvā-demons.

sanskrit: sahaḥ sahasvaty asi- -itaḥ kaṇvāḥ paro 'nudaḥ | imā yā adhunāgatā yāś ceha grahaṇīḥ purā ||
english: You are might, O mighty one; drive the Kaṇva-demons away hence, to the beyond. These that have just now arrived and those seizure-demons that were here before.

sanskrit: na tā itthā na tā ihāva māsatā ukheva śṛṅgavac chiraḥ | sadānvā brahmaṇaspate tīkṣṇaśṛṅgodṛṣann ihi ||
english: Let them not remain thus, let them not remain here. A head like a pot, like one with horns — O Bṛhaspati, come here, sharp-horned, looking down upon the sadānvā-demons.

sanskrit: vi te nu manthāḥ śaśrire bibhide te gadohanī | dadau te adya gauḥ kaṇve parehy avaraṃ mṛṇe ||
english: Your churning-rods have now been shattered; your milk-pail has been split. The cow has given to you today, O Kaṇva-demon. Withdraw; I crush what is lower.

sanskrit: yās tarke tiṣṭhanti yā valīke yāḥ preṅkhe preṅkhayanta uta yā nu ghorāḥ | yā garbhān pramṛśanti sarvāḥ pāpīr anīnaśam ||
english: Those that stand at the spindle, those at the wicker-frame, those that swing upon the swing, and those that are dreadful — those that harm the embryos: all those evil ones I have destroyed.

sanskrit: yāś celaṃ vasata uta yā nu dūrśaṃ nīlaṃ piśaṅgam uta lohitaṃ yāḥ | yā garbhān pramṛśanti sarvāḥ pāpīr anīnaśam ||
english: Those that dwell in garments and those that haunt distant places — the dark-blue ones, the tawny ones, and the red ones — those that harm the embryos: all those evil ones I have destroyed.

sanskrit: ākhidantīr vikhidantīḥ prāṇam asyāpi nahyata | durṇāmnīḥ sarvāḥ saṃgatya māmuṣyoc chiṣṭa kiṃ cana ||
english: Those that draw in and those that draw out — bind up his breath. Let all the ill-named ones assemble together and leave not a remnant of this man.
